## ✨ New Features

### Every contributor gets credit

Your release notes now name who did the work. Each pull request is listed with its author's GitHub handle, and people contributing for the first time get a New Contributors section. Your agent starts from that list instead of piecing it together from git history, and handles always come from GitHub, so nobody is credited under the wrong name. (#6)

## ⬆️ Improvements

### Catch release environment problems before they block a release

A misconfigured `release` environment used to surface only when a release failed to publish, or not at all. Now every release check warns you, without blocking, if your setup would stop your release branch from publishing, would let other branches publish, or requires reviewers who would hold every release for a second approval after you've already merged. Each warning links to the [setup steps](https://release-planner.fabricahq.com/start-here/set-up/#create-the-release-environment). (#7)

### Move your release notes without losing your history

You can now change where your release notes live and move the published ones along with them. Release Planner recognizes published notes that moved unchanged, and doesn't treat them as a new release. Notes that changed along the way are still refused. (#10)

### Also in this release

- The documentation is now at [release-planner.fabricahq.com](https://release-planner.fabricahq.com). (#8)
- [Set up a repository](https://release-planner.fabricahq.com/start-here/set-up/#create-the-release-environment) walks through creating the `release` environment. (#5)
- The config file explains that bumping `version` upgrades your Release workflow, `.github/workflows/release-planner.yml`. (#9)
- For tool authors: `release-planner inventory` now includes `authorHandle`, `newContributors`, and `warnings` in its JSON. (#6)

## ⛓️‍💥 Breaking Changes

### New release notes go in `_releases/`

If your config doesn't set `notes-dir`, Release Planner now looks for release notes in `_releases/` instead of `releases/`, which keeps them apart from your repository's own content. If your notes are in `releases/`, keep that directory or move it, as the upgrade steps explain. Otherwise your next release request would go unnoticed. (#10)

### The pull request list is now called Pull Requests

Release notes list pull requests under `## Pull Requests` instead of `## What's Changed`. If your release notes style or policy mentions What's Changed, rename it so your agent gets consistent instructions. (#6)

### Upgrade steps

1. Install v0.2.0:

   ```sh
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fabricahq/release-planner/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.2.0
   ```

2. Set `version: v0.2.0` in `.release-planner/config.yml`.
3. If your notes are in `releases/` and the config doesn't set `notes-dir`, either keep them there by adding `notes-dir: releases`, or move them with `git mv releases _releases`.
4. If your release notes style or policy mentions What's Changed, change it to Pull Requests.
5. Run `release-planner install` to update your Release workflow, agent guide, and release skill, then commit everything in one pull request.
